objective_for_doctor: A 54-year-old Male patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: I have lower chest pain, right side of the chest pain, and a knife stroke pain.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

I have lower chest pain on the right side—like a knife-stab feeling. It’s been pretty bad, around 7 out of 10, and it started fairly fast, maybe within minutes. Also I feel short of breath and I get palpitations, and it’s worse when I lie flat (I have orthopnea). I recently had a viral infection too, and I’ve been feeling more tired and achy in general.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—when did this start exactly, and is the pain worse with breathing in or with movement/pressing on your chest?  
Doctor: Do you have fever, cough, leg swelling/pain, or have you noticed any dizziness or fainting?

It started fairly quickly—within about minutes of onset—so the speed is around 5/10. The pain feels sharp like a knife, but I don’t know if it’s worse with breathing in; and I’m not sure if it gets worse when pressing on my chest or moving.  

I don’t have fever or cough that I’ve noticed, and I haven’t noticed any leg swelling or leg pain. I also haven’t had dizziness or fainting.

Doctor: Any history of heart disease, prior blood clots, smoking, recent long travel/immobility, or cancer—and does your oxygen feel low or have you had any sweating/nausea with the pain?  
Doctor: I need to rule out dangerous causes—REQUEST TEST: ECG and REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray.

I don’t have a known history of heart disease, prior blood clots, or cancer. I haven’t had recent long travel or any big immobility. I’m not sure about smoking—I can’t say for sure right now.  

I don’t know if my oxygen feels low, and I haven’t noticed sweating or nausea with the pain. Yes, you can do the ECG and the chest X-ray.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—while we wait for the ECG and chest X-ray, can you tell me your age and whether the pain is constant or comes in waves, and if you have pain relief with sitting up or antacids?  
Doctor: Also, any recent bleeding, new medications, or a strong family history of sudden cardiac death or clotting disorders?

I’m 54 years old. The pain is not completely constant—it kind of comes and goes in waves, but it’s been overall pretty bad. Sitting up seems to help a little, but I haven’t tried antacids yet.  

I haven’t had any recent bleeding, and I’m not aware of any new medications. I don’t know my family history of sudden cardiac death or clotting disorders.

Doctor: Thanks—given your sudden sharp right-sided chest pain with shortness of breath/orthopnea and palpitations, I’m concerned about a cardiopulmonary cause (including pulmonary embolism or cardiac ischemia); do you have any recent leg swelling, hemoptysis, or worsening symptoms with deep breaths?  
Doctor: Also, are you able to rate your heart rate when it happens (fast/regular vs irregular), and did the viral illness occur in the last 1–4 weeks?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: D-dimer and REQUEST TEST: Troponin (high-sensitivity)

I haven’t noticed any leg swelling and I don’t have hemoptysis. I’m not sure if it’s worse with deep breaths.  

My heart rate feels fast when it happens, but I can’t tell if it’s regular or irregular. The viral illness was fairly recent—within the last few weeks (about 1–4 weeks). Yes, you can do the D-dimer and the high-sensitivity troponin.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—while we wait for the D-dimer and high-sensitivity troponin, do you have any oxygen saturation reading at home/clinic or any severe worsening with coughing or taking a deep breath?  
Doctor: Also, on a 0–10 scale is the pain getting worse over time, and do you have any risk factors like smoking, hormone/testosterone use, or known heart rhythm problems?

I don’t have an oxygen saturation reading at home or here. I haven’t noticed severe worsening with coughing, but I’m not sure about deep breath—my breathing feels difficult overall because of the shortness of breath.  

On a 0–10 scale, it feels like it’s been about the same but still very bad around 7/10, not steadily getting worse. I’m not sure about smoking, testosterone/hormone use, or any known heart rhythm problems.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—right now your combination of sudden sharp chest pain, shortness of breath/orthopnea, and palpitations keeps me worried about time-sensitive causes like pulmonary embolism or cardiac ischemia/myocarditis after a recent viral illness. While we await results, I want a physical exam: I’ll check your vitals (including oxygen saturation), do a lung/heart exam, and assess for chest-wall tenderness and signs of DVT—are you currently able to sit up and can you tell me your current blood pressure and heart rate if you have them?  
Doctor: Also, please answer quickly: have you had any new wheezing or cough, and are you able to take one deep breath without severe pain?

I can sit up. I don’t have my current blood pressure or heart rate reading right now—I haven’t been checking it.  

I haven’t noticed new wheezing or a cough. I can take a deep breath, but it feels very uncomfortable because my breathing is already difficult, and I’m not sure I can do it fully without pain.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—given the acute pleuritic-type sharp chest pain with shortness of breath/orthopnea and recent viral illness, I’m treating this as potentially life-threatening until proven otherwise; I need STAT vitals (oxygen saturation, heart rate, blood pressure, respiratory rate) and a focused bedside exam right now.  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: CT_Pulmonary_Angiography (or V/Q scan if contraindicated) and REQUEST TEST: Basic_Metabolic_Panel/CBC (and repeat troponin in 1–3 hours if not already done).  
Doctor: If your oxygen is low, your heart rate is very fast, or symptoms are worsening, you should go to the ER immediately—are you currently in a clinic with monitoring available?

I’m in the Emergency Department/clinic area where you can monitor me. I don’t have my oxygen saturation, heart rate, blood pressure, or respiratory rate numbers right now. If you want, you can check them right away—I’m feeling pretty short of breath and the pain is still very intense.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—please let me check your vitals now: oxygen saturation, heart rate, blood pressure, and respiratory rate, and I’ll do a focused lung/heart exam and check for chest-wall tenderness and leg swelling.  
Doctor: Also, are you having any fainting, new confusion, blue lips, or coughing up blood right now?

I’m not fainting, and I’m not confused. I don’t have blue lips, and I’m not coughing up blood.  

I don’t have the vitals numbers myself—please check them now.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—REQUEST TEST: Vital_signs_now (SpO2, HR, BP, RR). While that’s happening, I’m also going to do a focused exam for lung sounds, heart rhythm, oxygen need, and any leg swelling/tenderness.  
Doctor: One more quick question: do you have any leg swelling on either side right now, and is the chest pain clearly worse when you take a deep breath (pleuritic)?

No—no leg swelling on either side right now.  

And the chest pain might be worse with a deep breath, but I can’t say for sure; breathing is already uncomfortable because I’m short of breath.

Doctor: Thanks—no leg swelling is noted, but your likely pleuritic sharp chest pain with shortness of breath/orthopnea after a recent viral illness still requires urgent rule-out of pulmonary embolism and cardiac causes. Can you tell me your vital signs right now (SpO₂, HR, BP, RR), and is your heart rate fast and regular or irregular?  
Doctor: If you have your ECG result or can get it immediately, request it and also tell me whether the troponin came back elevated.

I don’t have the vital sign numbers right now, and I can’t see the monitors.  

My heart rate feels fast when it happens, but I can’t tell if it’s regular or irregular. I haven’t gotten the ECG or troponin results yet—please check and tell me what they show.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—since I still don’t have your SpO₂, BP, RR, ECG, or troponin, I can’t safely diagnose you yet, but your sudden sharp chest pain with shortness of breath/orthopnea after a recent viral illness is still high-risk for pulmonary embolism, myocarditis/pericarditis, or acute coronary syndrome. REQUEST TEST: STAT_ECG_now and REQUEST TEST: STAT_Troponin_and_D_dimer_results and REQUEST TEST: CT_Pulmonary_Angiography_now (or V/Q if contraindicated), then immediately tell me the oxygen saturation and whether it’s hypoxic.
I understand. I’m still very short of breath and the chest pain is still intense. I don’t have my oxygen saturation number, but please check the monitor right now and tell me if I’m hypoxic.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—while you’re on the monitor, I need your **SpO₂, HR, BP, and RR right now**, and immediately afterward I will interpret the **ECG** and **troponin/D-dimer** to decide next steps.  
Doctor: Are you **hypoxic** (SpO₂ < 90% or < 94% depending on the local threshold) right now, and does the ECG show **ST changes/arrhythmia**?
I can’t see the monitor numbers, so I can’t tell you my SpO₂, HR, BP, or RR right now. I also don’t have the ECG results myself—please read them off when you’re done.

Doctor: I can’t safely proceed to a diagnosis without your actual oxygen saturation, blood pressure, respiratory rate, and ECG/troponin findings—please let staff tell me **SpO₂, HR, BP, RR immediately** and have them confirm whether the **ECG shows ST-segment changes or a significant arrhythmia**.  
Doctor: Also, REQUEST TEST: Repeat_high_sensitivity_Troponin_in_1_to_3_hours (if not already resulted) and REQUEST TEST: CT_Pulmonary_Angiography_now (or V/Q if contrast contraindicated), then tell me whether the **troponin is elevated** and whether **D-dimer is positive**.

I can’t provide the SpO₂, HR, BP, or RR numbers or confirm what the ECG shows, because I can’t see the monitor/ECG readout from where I am.  

Please proceed with the STAT tests (repeat high-sensitivity troponin, CT pulmonary angiography or V/Q, and tell me if troponin is elevated and whether D-dimer is positive) and I’ll follow whatever you decide next.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—given your inability to share vital/ECG data and your high-risk symptom cluster (sudden sharp pleuritic-type right chest pain + shortness of breath/orthopnea + palpitations after recent viral illness), I’m proceeding as if this could be **pulmonary embolism or acute cardiac inflammation/ischemia** until proven otherwise.  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: STAT_CTPA_or_VQ (pulmonary embolism protocol) + REQUEST TEST: STAT_High_sensitivity_Troponin_now_and_repeat_in_1-3_hours + REQUEST TEST: STAT_D_dimer + REQUEST TEST: STAT_ECG_now.  
Doctor: DIAGNOSIS READY: **Undifferentiated high-risk chest pain—rule out Pulmonary Embolism and Acute Coronary Syndrome/Myocarditis (pending STAT ECG/troponin/D-dimer and CTPA/VQ).**

[DDX]
1. Myocarditis
2. Pulmonary embolism
